# EvalDelta: benchmark results

**Status: final for v0.1.0, revision 2 (4 source families).** Generated by
`python benchmarks/analyze_results.py --suffix v2 --out-suffix v2` from
`results/frozen/{test_cpu_v2,nullreal_cpu_v2,ablate_cpu_v2,test_transfer_v2,nullreal_transfer_v2}`.
Public aggregate tables: `results/frozen/analysis/*_v2.csv`, `comparisons_v2.json`; row-level trial files are not redistributed. Figures:
`docs/figures/*v2.png`. The original 3-source run (`*_v1` files, no suffix) is kept for
comparison and is referenced explicitly in §2 below — it is **not** the current result.

**What changed since revision 1:** a fourth real, free dataset (UCI Bank Marketing, via OpenML,
`benchmarks/prepare_real.py --sources bank`) was added to tighten the source-family bootstrap and
stress-test the revision-1 findings. `PairedShift` was retrained on the resulting 48-episode
historical-train split (`configs/paired_shift_model.json`) and the full validation → freeze →
held-out-test pipeline was rerun end to end. `configs/frozen.yaml` was re-frozen from validation
data only, but unlike revision 1 that freeze was not committed before the rerun and the old test pairs had
already been seen — see §5b before treating revision 2 as a pristine held-out test. Both
revisions' settings and code hashes are recorded in the archived
`docs/run_manifests/*.json` files (and regenerated locally in each run's `manifest.json`).

Do not read this document as a benchmark leaderboard: four source families (Adult, Covertype,
AG News, Bank Marketing) and one held-out transfer family (CIFAR-10) is still a small evidence
base. Every "budget" below is the maximum paid candidate evaluations; every rate is over the
stated number of (source, version-pair, injected-scenario) combinations x seeds.

## 1. Empirical calibration on these scenarios

`results/frozen/analysis/null_boundary_v2.csv` (revision 1: `null_boundary.csv`): on real held-out
test pairs, with the regression margin set to each pair's own true Δ (the hardest boundary case),
observed false-alarm rates at α = 0.05 range from **0.04% to 2.35%** across method x budget x
family in revision 2 (revision 1: 0.19% to 2.11%). The two ranges are comparable, not "tighter":
the largest rate in both is `B8_seq_betting_wor` at budget 1000 (2.11% -> 2.35%). For the proposed
method, `OURS2_paired_shift_ipw` on the CPU families: 0.28% / 1.37% at budgets 200 / 1000 in
revision 1 and 0.07% / 0.99% in revision 2. Every observed rate is below 5% in these repeated-seed scenarios. These observations
do not prove error control beyond the protocol assumptions or across independent datasets.

Slice family: in every trial in the slice-detection tables (both revisions), zero confirmed slices
had a true Δ at or below the margin (`false_slice_confirmations` sums to 0). Note this counts
false confirmations of *non-target* slices in episodes that have an injected target slice; the
all-slices-null case is covered by the synthetic calibration in `docs/CALIBRATION.md`
(`D_slices`, 3/400 family-wise false alarms, 95% CI [0.2%, 2.2%]).

## 2. Global regression detection: the 3-source "advantage" did not survive a 4th source

This is the most important update in this revision. `global_real_v2.csv`, `comparisons_v2.json`.

| Budget | `OURS2_paired_shift_ipw` vs `B1_fixed_mcnemar` — **3 sources (rev. 1)** | **4 sources (rev. 2, this doc)** |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | -0.6pp (16.5% vs 17.1%), 95% CI [-7.9, +10.0] pp | **-2.9pp** (14.2% vs 17.1%), 95% CI [-10.0, +4.8] pp |
| 500 | **+5.9pp** (47.6% vs 41.8%), 95% CI [-8.6, +23.3] pp | **+2.5pp** (42.7% vs 40.2%), 95% CI [-7.3, +14.0] pp |

Adding one more real, independently-built dataset **shrank the budget-500 effect by more than
half (+5.9pp -> +2.5pp)** and made the already slightly negative budget-200 difference somewhat
more negative (-0.6pp -> -2.9pp; the sign was negative in both revisions). All four confidence
intervals comfortably cross zero. The added source shows how sensitive the earlier estimate was to the small number of source families. The conclusion is: there is no statistically reliable evidence that
`OURS2_paired_shift_ipw` detects real regressions more efficiently than a fixed-sample McNemar
baseline at a matched budget, on this benchmark, at this scale of evidence. It may still be true
with more source families; it is not established with four.

On the **held-out transfer family** (CIFAR-10, unchanged from revision 1 since no new vision data
was added), the result is essentially the same as before: no advantage, single source family so no
meaningful bootstrap CI. At budget 500: OURS2 28.6% vs B1 29.5% (-0.9pp). At budget 200: OURS2
26.8% vs B1 30.5% (-3.6pp).

## 3. Slice-regression triage: no improvement between revisions

`slice_injected.csv` (rev. 1) and `slice_injected_v2.csv` (rev. 2), CPU test split, target-slice
confirmation rate. **Both revisions used the same slice-ranking heuristic (`slice_rank:
residual_z`)**: it was selected on validation data (`validate2`) before the revision-1 held-out
run and is present in the committed revision-1 config (`48461e6`). Nothing about the ranking
changed between revisions; only the source set, the retrained historical model and the
re-frozen hyperparameters did.

| Budget | `paired_shift` rev. 1 | `uniform` rev. 1 | `stratified` rev. 1 | `paired_shift` rev. 2 | `uniform` rev. 2 | `stratified` rev. 2 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 300 | 47.8% | 52.2% | 51.1% | 45.2% | 49.8% | 49.8% |
| 600 | 71.4% | 73.1% | 75.3% | 71.7% | 71.5% | 72.3% |
| 1000 | 84.4% | 86.4% | 86.4% | 82.1% | 83.8% | 85.4% |

`paired_shift` is at or below `uniform` in five of six budget/revision cells (-4.4, -1.7, -2.0
pp in revision 1; -4.6, +0.2, -1.7 pp in revision 2). The single "tie" at budget 600 in revision 2
comes from `uniform` falling from 73.1% to 71.5% on the changed episode set, not from
`paired_shift` improving (71.4% -> 71.7%). Differences of a few percentage points here are within
Monte Carlo noise of 360-480 correlated trials and are not tested at the source-family level.

On the transfer family the ordering is the same in both revisions: `uniform` / `stratified` ahead
of `paired_shift` (revision 2, budget 600: 96.7% / 98.3% vs 91.7%).

**Conclusion (unchanged from revision 1):** `PairedShift` slice-triage does not beat plain random
or stratified-random discovery on this benchmark. `uniform` / `stratified` remain the recommended
default for slice discovery.

## 4. Ablations (unchanged from revision 1; ran only on the 4-source `ablate_cpu_v2` set)

See `results/frozen/ablate_cpu_v2/trials.parquet`. Qualitative findings are unchanged from
revision 1: the control variate helps the global method, too little exploration (ε=0.05) hurts,
and the budget-fraction split matters more than any single acquisition hyperparameter. The
"hand-set prior sometimes beats the trained model" ablation flag was seen in revision 1; it has
not been re-checked cell-by-cell for revision 2 in this document and is not used to change the
frozen model.

## 5b. Provenance caveat for revision 2

Revision 1's freeze is backed by git (`48461e6`, committed before held-out runs). Revision 2's
re-freeze (`configs/frozen.yaml` written 16:31 UTC, held-out runs started 16:34 UTC) is evidenced
by file timestamps and each run's `manifest.json` hashes, **not** by a commit made before the run. Also, the
Adult/Covertype/AG News held-out test pairs in revision 2 are the same ones already seen in
revision 1, and the decision to add a fourth source and retrain was made after seeing revision-1
held-out results. The retraining and hyperparameter selection themselves used only historical-train
and validation episodes, but revision 2 is a robustness re-run, not a pristine second held-out
test. Only the Bank Marketing episodes are new to both stages.

## 6. What this benchmark does not show

Four source families is still not enough to generalise "adaptive paired testing saves budget" as a
domain-general claim, and revision 2's main finding is that it is *less* supported than revision 1
suggested, not more. The transfer result remains a single held-out family. See
`docs/STATISTICAL_PROTOCOL.md` §9 and `docs/BENCHMARK_CARD.md` for standing limitations.

## 7. Release interpretation

* **The statistical core is tested under its stated assumptions**: the sealed
  discovery/confirmation design and budget accounting have tests, and observed null
  calibration is consistent with the 5% target in these benchmark scenarios (§1).
* **`OURS2`/`AdaptiveGlobalPlan` has no demonstrated efficiency win.** Two
  revisions of this benchmark, with 3 and then 4 source families, both produced confidence
  intervals crossing zero and inconsistent signs across budgets. It remains available as an
  opt-in research feature.
* **`PairedShift` slice triage did not outperform the simple baselines.** `uniform` and
  `stratified` remain the default discovery policies; `paired_shift` is an opt-in research option.
* When quoting a result, include its revision, budget, source family and uncertainty. A bare
  percentage improvement would hide the wide source-level interval.
